newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Nov export orders down 4.16 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Nov export orders down 4.16 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods fell 4.16 percent in November to US$10.027 billion compared to November 1995, the economics ministry said on Friday.
The following is a table of export data in million of U.S. dollars.
The ministry attributed November's decline in orders to an unusually high basis in 1995, when orders were peaking at exceptionally high levels.
It said the fact that Taiwan's monthly export orders have exceeded T$10 billion for four consecutive months would help contribute to steady future growth.

Geographically, the worst news was for orders from the United States, which fell 14.01 percent to $2.798 billion as orders for information and telecommunication products -- Taiwan's most promising industrial sectors -- declined.
November orders in information and telecommunication products decreased 19.24 percent to $1.469 billion and electronics orders fell 5.05 percent to $1.448 billion.
November orders from Hong Kong edged up 1.10 percent to $2.014 billion, while orders from Japan were down 2.48 percent to $1.296 billion.
European orders were a bright spot, rising 9.27 percent to $1.627 billion, with electronics, telecommunication and information products orders accounting for the main rise.
In sectoral terms, textile orders were down 1.27 percent to $1.246 billion and base metal products orders decreased 8.52 percent to $795 million.
Machinery orders grew 9.45 percent to $718 million.
Plastics and rubber products orders were down 13.59 percent to $617 million.
Orders for transportation tools and equipment were down 32.43 percent to $375 million.
